narrative: Material PL1__M450F85A exhibits erratic daily demand (CV=0.58) with a slight upward trend across the observation window (March 2025 to March 2026). Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.51), contributing 65.9% of the combined demand-lead-time variance, making buffer sizing the dominant risk driver. The recommended (r,Q) policy with safety stock of 1,753 units and order quantity of 6,274 units (capacity-constrained from unconstrained EOQ of 12,776) delivers 95% service level while reducing annual costs by 71.5% through dramatic consolidation of order frequency from ~128 to ~27 orders per year.
warnings: Order quantity capped at 6,274 units due to max_storage_units constraint (8,027). Unconstrained EOQ was 12,776 units. Capacity constraint reduces holding cost efficiency.
Slight upward demand trend detected — review safety stock levels in 6 months if trend persists.

research_insights.selection_rationale: With 93.1% non-zero demand days and erratic but not intermittent demand, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is appropriate. The trigger-based reorder mechanism provides responsive stock-out protection without the excess cycle-stock overhead of periodic-review systems. EOQ minimises total cost given the low unit cost and moderate ordering cost.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 8,027 units binds the EOQ calculation, reducing order quantity from 12,776 to 6,274 units. This reduces the ordering cost advantage (more frequent orders than unconstrained optimum) and may require renegotiation of warehouse allocation or supplier delivery cadence if demand trends upward.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (1,343) + safety_stock (1,753) = 3,096 <= max_storage_units (8,027). Policy is feasible.
